name: Adi Shankaracharya
tagline: The prodigy monk who walked the length of India to revive Vedanta.
journey: Shankara set out on foot across the Indian subcontinent. He debated scholars, established four Mathas, and synthesized intellect and devotion under Advaita Vedanta.
trial: He faced fierce opposition, survived assassination attempts, and broke orthodox rules to perform his mother's last rites, proving compassion supersedes dogma.
teaching: Brahma Satyam Jagan Mithya Jivo Brahmaiva Na Aparah.
moral: True knowledge reveals the underlying unity in all diversity.
journey_local: शंकर ने पूरे भारतीय उपमहाद्वीप की पैदल यात्रा की। उन्होंने चार मठों की स्थापना की और अद्वैत वेदांत के तहत बुद्धि और भक्ति को संश्लेषित किया।
trial_local: उन्होंने रूढ़िवादियों के कड़े विरोध का सामना किया और अपनी माँ का अंतिम संस्कार करने के लिए संन्यास के नियमों को तोड़ दिया।
teaching_local: ब्रह्म सत्य है, जगत मिथ्या है, और जीव ब्रह्म से भिन्न नहीं है।
moral_local: सच्चा ज्ञान सभी विविधताओं में अंतर्निहित एकता को प्रकट करता है।

name: Akali Phula Singh
tagline: The fearless Nihang leader who became the moral compass of the Sikh Empire.
journey: The head of the Akal Takht and leader of the Nihang warriors. He was known for his absolute fearlessness and strict adherence to the Khalsa code. He did not hesitate to publicly flog Maharaja Ranjit Singh for a moral transgression, treating the mighty Emperor as an ordinary citizen before the eyes of the Guru. Ranjit Singh humbly accepted the punishment.
trial: His trial was speaking truth to absolute power. He fought on the frontlines of the Empire's toughest battles (Multan, Kashmir, Naushera), eventually achieving martyrdom in combat, proving that a true saint-soldier fights with the sword, but serves only the truth.
teaching: No king is above the discipline of the Khalsa.
moral: Integrity means holding the powerful accountable to the same rules as the powerless.
journey_local: ਅਕਾਲ ਤਖ਼ਤ ਦੇ ਜਥੇਦਾਰ ਅਤੇ ਨਿਹੰਗ ਯੋਧਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਆਗੂ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਮਹਾਰਾਜਾ ਰਣਜੀਤ ਸਿੰਘ ਨੂੰ ਵੀ ਧਾਰਮਿਕ ਉਲੰਘਣਾ ਲਈ ਸਜ਼ਾ ਦਿੱਤੀ।
trial_local: ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰੀਖਿਆ ਪੂਰਨ ਸ਼ਕਤੀ ਦੇ ਸਾਹਮਣੇ ਸੱਚ ਬੋਲਣਾ ਸੀ। ਉਹ ਸਾਮਰਾਜ ਦੀਆਂ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਮੁਸ਼ਕਲ ਲੜਾਈਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਮੂਹਰਲੀ ਕਤਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਲੜੇ।
teaching_local: ਕੋਈ ਵੀ ਰਾਜਾ ਖਾਲਸੇ ਦੇ ਅਨੁਸ਼ਾਸਨ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਪਰ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ।
moral_local: ਸੱਚਾਈ ਦਾ ਅਰਥ ਹੈ ਤਾਕਤਵਰ ਨੂੰ ਵੀ ਉਹੀ ਨਿਯਮਾਂ ਦੇ ਜਵਾਬਦੇਹ ਠਹਿਰਾਉਣਾ ਜੋ ਕਮਜ਼ੋਰ ਲਈ ਹਨ।

name: Ananda
tagline: The devoted attendant who remembered every word of the Buddha.
journey: Ananda was the Buddha's first cousin and served as his personal attendant for 25 years. He possessed an extraordinary memory and memorized the vast majority of the Buddha's discourses. After the Buddha's passing, Ananda was crucial at the First Buddhist Council, reciting the Suttas which begin with the famous phrase "Thus have I heard." He was also instrumental in convincing the Buddha to establish the order of nuns (Bhikkhunis).
trial: Despite his closeness to the Buddha, Ananda was the last of the core disciples to attain enlightenment, achieving it only the night before the First Council out of sheer desperate meditation, proving that proximity to greatness is not a substitute for personal practice.
teaching: Thus have I heard (Evam me sutam).
moral: Perfect service and deep listening are forms of profound spiritual practice.
journey_local: आनंद बुद्ध के चचेरे भाई थे और 25 वर्षों तक उनके व्यक्तिगत परिचारक के रूप में कार्य किया। उनके पास एक असाधारण स्मृति थी और उन्होंने बुद्ध के अधिकांश प्रवचनों को याद कर लिया था।
trial_local: बुद्ध से निकटता के बावजूद, आनंद सबसे अंत में ज्ञान प्राप्त करने वाले शिष्यों में से थे। उन्होंने साबित किया कि महानता के करीब होना व्यक्तिगत अभ्यास का विकल्प नहीं है।
teaching_local: ऐसा मैंने सुना है (एवं मे सुतं)।
moral_local: पूर्ण सेवा और गहरा श्रवण गहरे आध्यात्मिक अभ्यास के रूप हैं।

name: Arjuna
tagline: The peerless archer whose moment of profound doubt gave humanity the Bhagavad Gita.
journey: The third Pandava prince, Arjuna was the greatest warrior of his time, possessing laser-like focus. Right before the great war of Kurukshetra, seeing his grand-uncle, teacher, and cousins in the enemy ranks, he dropped his bow in moral paralysis.
trial: His trial was the ultimate existential crisis: choose between family loyalty and universal Dharma. Only through Krishna's divine discourse did he pick up his bow again.
teaching: Wherever there is Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, and Arjuna, the supreme archer, there will be prosperity, victory, and sound policy.
moral: Doubt is the beginning of wisdom; seeking guidance from the Divine leads to righteous action.
journey_local: तीसरे पांडव राजकुमार, अर्जुन कुरुक्षेत्र के युद्ध से ठीक पहले नैतिक पक्षाघात में पड़ गए।
trial_local: उनका परीक्षण अंतिम अस्तित्वगत संकट था: पारिवारिक वफादारी और सार्वभौमिक धर्म के बीच चयन करना।
teaching_local: जहाँ योगेश्वर कृष्ण और धनुर्धर अर्जुन हैं, वहाँ निश्चित ही विजय और ऐश्वर्य है।
moral_local: संदेह ज्ञान की शुरुआत है; परमात्मा से मार्गदर्शन प्राप्त करने से धर्मी कार्य होता है।

name: Atisha Dipankara Srijnana
tagline: The great scholar-monk of Vikramashila who crossed the Himalayas to revive pure Buddhism in Tibet.
journey: Atisha was one of the major figures in the spread of Mahayana and Vajrayana Buddhism. Despite his advanced age and the immense dangers of the Himalayan crossing, he accepted the invitation of the Tibetan king to reform Tibetan Buddhism, which had fallen into degenerate practices. He wrote the "Lamp for the Path to Enlightenment," synthesizing the stages of the path.
trial: He gave up his prestigious position at India's greatest university and risked his life in the frozen mountains purely out of compassion for the Tibetan people who lacked clear spiritual guidance.
teaching: The greatest achievement is selflessness. The greatest worth is self-mastery. The greatest quality is seeking to serve others.
moral: True scholarship is not measured by academic titles, but by the willingness to serve where you are most needed.
journey_local: अतीश ने तिब्बती बौद्ध धर्म में सुधार करने के लिए तिब्बती राजा के निमंत्रण को स्वीकार किया, जो पतित प्रथाओं में गिर गया था। उन्होंने "ज्ञान के मार्ग के लिए दीपक" लिखा।
trial_local: उन्होंने भारत के सबसे महान विश्वविद्यालय में अपना प्रतिष्ठित पद छोड़ दिया और तिब्बती लोगों के लिए करुणा के कारण बर्फीले पहाड़ों में अपनी जान जोखिम में डाल दी।
teaching_local: सबसे बड़ी उपलब्धि निस्वार्थता है। सबसे बड़ा मूल्य आत्म-नियंत्रण है। सबसे बड़ा गुण दूसरों की सेवा करना है।
moral_local: सच्ची विद्वता अकादमिक उपाधियों से नहीं मापी जाती है, बल्कि सेवा करने की इच्छा से मापी जाती है।

name: Baba Deep Singh Ji
tagline: The scholar-warrior who fought to his dying breath to free the Golden Temple from desecration.
journey: A profound scholar who spent his life writing copies of the Guru Granth Sahib, Baba Deep Singh was in his seventies when word arrived that the Afghan invader Jahan Khan had destroyed and defiled the Harmandir Sahib. Enraged, he drew a line in the dirt with his heavy double-edged sword (khanda), asking only those ready to die to cross it and march with him to Amritsar.
trial: During the fierce battle, he sustained a fatal blow to the neck. Supporting his severed head with one hand and wielding his massive sword with the other, he miraculously fought his way to the perimeter of the Golden Temple to fulfill his vow before finally breathing his last.
teaching: My head may fall, but my faith must not fall.
moral: A vow made to the Divine gives the human body strength far beyond biological limits.
journey_local: ਇੱਕ ਮਹਾਨ ਵਿਦਵਾਨ, ਜਦੋਂ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਹਰਿਮੰਦਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦੀ ਬੇਅਦਬੀ ਬਾਰੇ ਪਤਾ ਲੱਗਾ, ਤਾਂ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਅੰਮ੍ਰਿਤਸਰ ਵੱਲ ਕੂਚ ਕੀਤਾ।
trial_local: ਗੰਭੀਰ ਜ਼ਖਮੀ ਹੋਣ ਦੇ ਬਾਵਜੂਦ, ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਆਪਣਾ ਸਿਰ ਇੱਕ ਹੱਥ ਵਿੱਚ ਫੜ ਕੇ ਲੜਾਈ ਜਾਰੀ ਰੱਖੀ ਅਤੇ ਹਰਿਮੰਦਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਪਹੁੰਚ ਕੇ ਆਪਣਾ ਪ੍ਰਣ ਪੂਰਾ ਕੀਤਾ।
teaching_local: ਸਿਰ ਜਾਵੇ ਤਾਂ ਜਾਵੇ, ਮੇਰਾ ਸਿੱਖੀ ਸਿਦਕ ਨਾ ਜਾਵੇ।
moral_local: ਪ੍ਰਮਾਤਮਾ ਨਾਲ ਕੀਤਾ ਪ੍ਰਣ ਮਨੁੱਖੀ ਸਰੀਰ ਨੂੰ ਜੀਵ-ਵਿਗਿਆਨਕ ਸੀਮਾਵਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਕਿਤੇ ਵੱਧ ਤਾਕਤ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ।

name: Lord Bahubali (Gommateshwara)
tagline: The invincible warrior who won the world but dropped his fist to conquer his own ego.
journey: Son of the first Tirthankara, Bahubali was challenged to a duel by his ambitious brother Bharata for supreme kingship. To avoid mass bloodshed, they engaged in a non-lethal one-on-one contest. Bahubali won easily, lifting his brother over his head. But realizing the madness of killing his own brother for a piece of earth, he gently set him down, plucked out his hair, and walked into the forest.
trial: He stood in Kayotsarga (standing meditation) for an entire year. Vines grew up his legs and anthills formed at his feet, but he could not attain omniscience because a tiny thorn of ego—"I am standing on my brother's land"—remained in his heart. Only when Bharata came and worshipped him did his ego dissolve, and he attained Kevala Jnana.
teaching: Ego is the only barrier between the soul and absolute freedom.
moral: True strength is not the power to destroy others, but the power to walk away from violence.
journey_local: पहले तीर्थंकर के पुत्र, बाहुबली को उनके भाई भरत ने युद्ध के लिए चुनौती दी थी। बाहुबली जीत गए, लेकिन अपने भाई को मारने के पागलपन को महसूस करते हुए, उन्होंने राज त्याग दिया।
trial_local: वे पूरे एक वर्ष तक कायोत्सर्ग (खड़े होकर ध्यान) में रहे, लेकिन उन्हें केवल ज्ञान प्राप्त नहीं हुआ क्योंकि उनके हृदय में अहंकार का एक कांटा था। जब भरत ने उनकी पूजा की तो उनका अहंकार दूर हो गया।
teaching_local: अहंकार आत्मा और पूर्ण स्वतंत्रता के बीच एकमात्र बाधा है।
moral_local: सच्ची ताकत दूसरों को नष्ट करने की शक्ति नहीं है, बल्कि हिंसा से दूर जाने की शक्ति है।

name: Banda Singh Bahadur
tagline: The ascetic-turned-general who shook the foundations of the Mughal Empire to establish the first Khalsa Raj.
journey: Madho Das was an ascetic with mystical powers. His life shifted when Guru Gobind Singh visited his ashram. Recognizing his true master, he submitted. Baptized as Banda Singh Bahadur, the Guru armed him and sent him to Punjab to end tyrannical rule. He mobilized the oppressed peasantry, captured Sirhind, established a sovereign state, and abolished the Zamindari system.
trial: Captured after an eight-month siege, he was offered a pardon if he converted. He refused. He witnessed his son's execution before being subjected to unspeakable torture. He remained calm to his last breath.
teaching: Dharma is justice for the powerless.
moral: Turn spiritual power into service for the oppressed.
journey_local: ਮਾਧੋ ਦਾਸ ਨਾਂਦੇੜ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਹਿਣ ਵਾਲੇ ਇੱਕ ਤਪੱਸਵੀ ਸਨ। ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਮਿਲਣ 'ਤੇ, ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਆਪ ਨੂੰ ਗੁਰੂ ਦਾ 'ਬੰਦਾ' ਕਿਹਾ। ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਪੰਜਾਬ ਭੇਜਿਆ।
trial_local: ਦਿੱਲੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਾਹਮਣੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਬੇਟੇ ਦਾ ਕਤਲ ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਗਿਆ, ਪਰ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਧਰਮ ਨਹੀਂ ਛੱਡਿਆ।
teaching_local: ਧਰਮ ਇਨਸਾਫ਼ ਹੈ — ਮਜ਼ਦੂਰ ਲਈ ਅਤੇ ਉਸ ਲਈ ਜਿਸ ਕੋਲ ਕੋਈ ਸ਼ਕਤੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ।
moral_local: ਆਪਣੀ ਅਧਿਆਤਮਿਕ ਸ਼ਕਤੀ ਨੂੰ ਸੇਵਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਬਦਲੋ।

name: Acharya Bhadrabahu
tagline: The last Shruta Kevali who led the great Jain migration south to preserve the ascetic tradition.
journey: Bhadrabahu was the last spiritual leader to have memorized the complete unwritten Jain scriptures (14 Purvas). Foreseeing a devastating twelve-year famine in North India, he led a massive migration of 12,000 monks to South India to protect the purity of their ascetic vows. The Mauryan Emperor Chandragupta renounced his throne to follow him as his disciple.
trial: His trial was abandoning the heartland of his faith and taking thousands into unknown territory solely to protect the uncompromising integrity of Jain monastic rules during a time of mass starvation.
teaching: Vows must not be compromised for convenience; physical survival is secondary to spiritual purity.
moral: A true leader foresees calamity and acts decisively to protect the truth, regardless of the hardship.
journey_local: भद्रबाहु अंतिम आध्यात्मिक नेता थे जिन्होंने संपूर्ण अलिखित जैन शास्त्रों को याद किया था। उन्होंने तपस्वी व्रतों की रक्षा के लिए 12,000 भिक्षुओं के दक्षिण भारत में प्रवास का नेतृत्व किया।
trial_local: उनका परीक्षण अपने धर्म के गढ़ को छोड़ना और भुखमरी के समय जैन मठवासी नियमों की अखंडता की रक्षा के लिए हजारों लोगों को अज्ञात क्षेत्र में ले जाना था।
teaching_local: सुविधा के लिए व्रतों से समझौता नहीं किया जाना चाहिए; आध्यात्मिक पवित्रता के सामने शारीरिक अस्तित्व गौण है।
moral_local: सच्चा नेता आपदा का पूर्वानुमान लगाता है और सत्य की रक्षा के लिए निर्णायक रूप से कार्य करता है।

name: Bhai Gurdas Ji
tagline: The intellectual giant whose writings act as the key to understanding the Guru Granth Sahib.
journey: A masterful scholar, poet, and the original scribe of the Adi Granth as dictated by Guru Arjan Dev Ji. He also served as a missionary, traveling widely to establish Sikh centers. His own poetic compositions (Vaaran) were so profound that Guru Arjan declared them to be the "key" to understanding the deep philosophical mysteries of the Sikh scripture.
trial: His trial was maintaining complete humility. Despite possessing intellect and spiritual knowledge rivaling the Gurus themselves, he always remained a subservient disciple, ensuring his own ego never eclipsed the divine word.
teaching: A Sikh is like a tree; it bears fruit only when it bows down in humility.
moral: True brilliance does not seek the spotlight; it acts as a lens to illuminate the truth.
journey_local: ਇੱਕ ਮਹਾਨ ਵਿਦਵਾਨ ਅਤੇ ਕਵੀ, ਜਿਸਨੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਅਰਜਨ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਨਿਰਦੇਸ਼ਾਂ ਹੇਠ ਆਦਿ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਲਿਖਿਆ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਵਾਰਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਗੁਰਬਾਣੀ ਦੀ "ਕੁੰਜੀ" ਮੰਨਿਆ ਜਾਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
trial_local: ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰੀਖਿਆ ਪੂਰਨ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਬਣਾਈ ਰੱਖਣਾ ਸੀ। ਅਪਾਰ ਗਿਆਨ ਹੋਣ ਦੇ ਬਾਵਜੂਦ, ਉਹ ਹਮੇਸ਼ਾ ਇੱਕ ਨਿਮਾਣੇ ਸੇਵਕ ਰਹੇ।
teaching_local: ਸਿੱਖ ਇੱਕ ਰੁੱਖ ਵਾਂਗ ਹੈ; ਇਹ ਉਦੋਂ ਹੀ ਫਲ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਹੈ ਜਦੋਂ ਇਹ ਨਿਮਰਤਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਝੁਕਦਾ ਹੈ।
moral_local: ਸੱਚੀ ਪ੍ਰਤਿਭਾ ਸੁਰਖੀਆਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਭਾਲਦੀ; ਇਹ ਸੱਚਾਈ ਨੂੰ ਰੌਸ਼ਨ ਕਰਨ ਲਈ ਇੱਕ ਲੈਂਸ ਵਜੋਂ ਕੰਮ ਕਰਦੀ ਹੈ।

name: Bhai Mani Singh Ji
tagline: The head granthi of the Golden Temple who was cut joint by joint but kept the Sikh congregation united.
journey: A profound scholar who served under Guru Gobind Singh and transcribed the final version of the Guru Granth Sahib. Later, as the Head Granthi of the Harmandir Sahib, he sought permission from the Mughal governor to hold a Diwali gathering, promising a large tax. When he realized the governor planned a secret attack on the unarmed gathering, he sent messages to cancel the event.
trial: Arrested for failing to pay the tax, he was sentenced to death by having his body dismembered joint by joint (band-band). As the executioner began at the wrist, Bhai Mani Singh calmly instructed him to start at the finger joints first, honoring the precise terms of his sentence without a flinch.
teaching: The body perishes, but the word of the Guru lives forever.
moral: Unshakable poise in the face of excruciating pain is the ultimate proof of spiritual mastery.
journey_local: ਗੁਰੂ ਗੋਬਿੰਦ ਸਿੰਘ ਜੀ ਦੇ ਅਧੀਨ ਸੇਵਾ ਕੀਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦਾ ਅੰਤਿਮ ਰੂਪ ਲਿਖਿਆ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਦੀਵਾਲੀ 'ਤੇ ਸਿੱਖਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਇਕੱਠਾ ਕਰਨ ਦੀ ਯੋਜਨਾ ਬਣਾਈ ਪਰ ਮੁਗਲ ਧੋਖੇ ਦਾ ਪਤਾ ਲੱਗਣ 'ਤੇ ਇਸਨੂੰ ਰੱਦ ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤਾ।
trial_local: ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਸਰੀਰ ਨੂੰ ਬੰਦ-ਬੰਦ (ਜੋੜ-ਜੋੜ) ਕੱਟਣ ਦੀ ਸਜ਼ਾ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਗਈ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਸ਼ਾਂਤੀ ਨਾਲ ਇਸਨੂੰ ਸਵੀਕਾਰ ਕੀਤਾ।
teaching_local: ਸਰੀਰ ਨਾਸ਼ਵਾਨ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਗੁਰੂ ਦਾ ਸ਼ਬਦ ਸਦਾ ਜਿਉਂਦਾ ਹੈ।
moral_local: ਅਸਹਿਣਸ਼ੀਲ ਦਰਦ ਦੇ ਸਾਹਮਣੇ ਅਟੁੱਟ ਸ਼ਾਂਤੀ ਅਧਿਆਤਮਿਕ ਮੁਹਾਰਤ ਦਾ ਅੰਤਮ ਸਬੂਤ ਹੈ।

name: Bhai Taru Singh Ji
tagline: The saintly farmer whose skull was removed, yet he refused to part with his faith or his hair.
journey: A simple, compassionate farmer who secretly provided food and shelter to Sikh fighters hiding in the jungles from Mughal persecution. He was betrayed by a village informant and arrested by Zakariya Khan.
trial: Offered pardon, wealth, and marriage if he converted to Islam and cut his hair, Taru Singh refused. Furious, the governor ordered his hair to be scraped off along with his scalp. Taru Singh endured the horrific torture while reciting Japji Sahib, proving that physical pain cannot conquer the soul.
teaching: My hair is part of my Guru's gift; it is not separate from my life.
moral: Identity is not just a symbol; it is an unbreakable covenant of love.
journey_local: ਇੱਕ ਸਾਧਾਰਨ ਕਿਸਾਨ ਜੋ ਜੰਗਲਾਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਲੁਕੇ ਸਿੱਖ ਯੋਧਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਭੋਜਨ ਦਿੰਦਾ ਸੀ। ਉਸਨੂੰ ਗ੍ਰਿਫਤਾਰ ਕਰ ਲਿਆ ਗਿਆ।
trial_local: ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਇਸਲਾਮ ਕਬੂਲਣ ਅਤੇ ਵਾਲ ਕੱਟਣ ਤੋਂ ਇਨਕਾਰ ਕਰ ਦਿੱਤਾ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਖੋਪੜੀ ਵਾਲਾਂ ਸਮੇਤ ਉਤਾਰ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਗਈ, ਪਰ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਜਪੁਜੀ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਦਾ ਪਾਠ ਜਾਰੀ ਰੱਖਿਆ।
teaching_local: ਸਿੱਖੀ ਕੇਸਾਂ ਸਵਾਸਾਂ ਨਾਲ ਨਿਭਾਉਣੀ ਹੈ।
moral_local: ਪਛਾਣ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਇੱਕ ਪ੍ਰਤੀਕ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ; ਇਹ ਪਿਆਰ ਦਾ ਇੱਕ ਅਟੁੱਟ ਨੇਮ ਹੈ।

name: Bhishma Pitamah
tagline: The grand patriarch of the Kuru clan whose terrifying vow bound him to a tragic destiny.
journey: Born as Devavrata, he took an unbreakable vow of lifelong celibacy and service to whoever sat on the throne of Hastinapur, just so his father could marry a fisherwoman. This terrible vow (Bhishma Pratigya) made him invincible, but also bound him to fight for the corrupt Kauravas in the great war.
trial: His trial was the agony of watching Dharma be destroyed by his own nephews, yet being forced by his vow to fight against the righteous Pandavas, ultimately lying on a bed of arrows to await an auspicious time to die.
teaching: A vow is sacred, but Dharma is contextually complex.
moral: Blind adherence to a rule, without considering the greater good, can lead to cosmic tragedy.
journey_local: उन्होंने आजीवन ब्रह्मचर्य और हस्तिनापुर के सिंहासन की सेवा करने की अटूट प्रतिज्ञा ली।
trial_local: उनकी परीक्षा अपनों द्वारा धर्म को नष्ट होते हुए देखने की पीड़ा थी।
teaching_local: एक प्रतिज्ञा पवित्र है, लेकिन धर्म प्रासंगिक रूप से जटिल है।
moral_local: अधिक भलाई पर विचार किए बिना एक नियम का अंधा पालन दुखद घटना का कारण बन सकता है।

name: Bodhidharma
tagline: The fierce Indian monk who transmitted Zen (Chan) Buddhism and martial arts to China.
journey: A prince from South India who became a monk, Bodhidharma traveled to China. When Emperor Wu boasted of building temples and translating texts, Bodhidharma bluntly told him these acts earned "no merit" because true Dhamma is beyond worldly accounting. He then retreated to a cave near the Shaolin Temple, where he sat facing a wall in meditation for nine years.
trial: His trial was transmitting the "mind-to-mind" seal of awakening in a foreign land obsessed with texts and rituals, sitting in absolute stillness until his legs allegedly withered away to prove the primacy of direct experience.
teaching: A special transmission outside the scriptures; No dependence upon words and letters; Direct pointing to the human mind; Seeing into one's nature and attaining Buddhahood.
moral: True understanding comes from looking inward, not from studying words.
journey_local: दक्षिण भारत के एक राजकुमार जो भिक्षु बने, बोधिधर्म ने चीन की यात्रा की। उन्होंने शाओलिन मंदिर के पास एक गुफा में नौ साल तक दीवार की ओर मुंह करके ध्यान किया।
trial_local: उनका परीक्षण ग्रंथों और अनुष्ठानों के प्रति जुनूनी एक विदेशी भूमि में जागृति को प्रसारित करना था, प्रत्यक्ष अनुभव की प्रधानता को साबित करने के लिए पूर्ण शांति में बैठे रहना।
teaching_local: शास्त्रों के बाहर एक विशेष प्रसारण; शब्दों पर कोई निर्भरता नहीं; मानव मन की ओर सीधा इशारा; अपने स्वभाव को देखना और बुद्धत्व प्राप्त करना।
moral_local: सच्ची समझ शब्दों के अध्ययन से नहीं, बल्कि भीतर देखने से आती है।

name: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
tagline: The architect of India's Constitution who revived Buddhism as a path to social equality (Navayana).
journey: Born into an "untouchable" caste, he faced horrific discrimination but rose to become one of India's greatest scholars and the architect of its Constitution. Believing that the caste system could not be reformed from within, he took refuge in Buddhism in 1956 along with half a million followers, sparking the Dalit Buddhist movement and reframing the Dhamma as an instrument of social justice.
trial: He endured a lifetime of systemic humiliation, yet he never resorted to violent revolution. He weaponized education, law, and eventually spiritual conversion to achieve dignity for millions.
teaching: I like the religion that teaches liberty, equality, and fraternity.
moral: Dharma must serve human dignity; a religion that sanctions inequality is no religion at all.
journey_local: एक "अछूत" जाति में जन्मे, उन्होंने भयानक भेदभाव का सामना किया लेकिन भारत के संविधान के निर्माता बने। १९५६ में, उन्होंने बौद्ध धर्म की शरण ली, जिससे दलित बौद्ध आंदोलन शुरू हुआ।
trial_local: उन्होंने जीवन भर व्यवस्थित अपमान सहा, फिर भी उन्होंने कभी हिंसक क्रांति का सहारा नहीं लिया। उन्होंने लाखों लोगों के लिए गरिमा प्राप्त करने के लिए शिक्षा और कानून का इस्तेमाल किया।
teaching_local: मुझे वह धर्म पसंद है जो स्वतंत्रता, समानता और बंधुत्व सिखाता है।
moral_local: धर्म को मानव गरिमा की सेवा करनी चाहिए; जो धर्म असमानता को मंजूरी देता है वह कोई धर्म नहीं है।

name: Chanakya (Kautilya)
tagline: The ascetic scholar who envisioned a united India and orchestrated the rise of the Mauryan Empire.
journey: Insulted by the Nanda dynasty, he vowed to uproot the corrupt empire. He trained Chandragupta and authored the Arthashastra, laying down principles of Dharma-based statecraft.
trial: He held the power of an emperor but lived in a mud hut, choosing cold strategy over personal glory.
teaching: In the happiness of his subjects lies the king's happiness.
moral: Power should be an instrument of service and order.
journey_local: नंद वंश द्वारा अपमानित होने पर, उन्होंने भ्रष्ट साम्राज्य को उखाड़ फेंकने की शपथ ली।
trial_local: एक सम्राट की शक्ति होने के बावजूद वे एक झोपड़ी में रहते थे।
teaching_local: प्रजा के सुख में ही राजा का सुख है।
moral_local: सत्ता सेवा और व्यवस्था का साधन होनी चाहिए।

name: Sadhvi Chandanbala
tagline: The enslaved princess who broke Mahavira's 5-month fast with a handful of lentils and immense devotion.
journey: A beautiful princess whose kingdom was destroyed, Vasumati was sold into slavery, tortured, and starved by a jealous mistress. Her head was shaved and her feet chained. Lord Mahavira had taken a nearly impossible vow to accept food only from a chained, starving princess who offered it with tears of joy. When Mahavira arrived at her door, she wept with pure devotion and offered him her meager dry lentils. Her chains shattered miraculously.
trial: Her trial was enduring horrific abuse, loss of status, and near-starvation without losing her innate capacity for devotion and selfless giving.
teaching: Purity of heart is more powerful than any worldly chain.
moral: In the eyes of the divine, the intention behind the offering is greater than the offering itself.
journey_local: एक खूबसूरत राजकुमारी जिसका राज्य नष्ट हो गया था, उसे गुलामी में बेच दिया गया और प्रताड़ित किया गया। उसने मुट्ठी भर दाल के साथ महावीर का उपवास तोड़ा।
trial_local: उनका परीक्षण भयानक दुर्व्यवहार, स्थिति की हानि और लगभग भुखमरी को सहना था, बिना अपनी भक्ति और निस्वार्थ देने की क्षमता को खोए।
teaching_local: हृदय की पवित्रता किसी भी सांसारिक जंजीर से अधिक शक्तिशाली होती है।
moral_local: ईश्वर की दृष्टि में, अर्पण के पीछे का इरादा अर्पण से बड़ा होता है।

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj
tagline: The visionary leader who established Hindavi Swarajya against impossible odds.
journey: Taking the oath of Swarajya at 16, he built a disciplined military, revived naval power, and pioneered guerrilla warfare. He was a just ruler who respected all faiths.
trial: From the encounter with Afzal Khan to his escape from Agra, his life was constantly on the line.
teaching: A kingdom is built for the protection and prosperity of the people.
moral: Vision, backed by tactical brilliance and moral integrity, can move mountains.
journey_local: १६ वर्ष की आयु में स्वराज्य की शपथ लेते हुए, उन्होंने हिंदवी स्वराज्य की स्थापना की।
trial_local: अफजल खान के साथ मुठभेड़ से लेकर आगरा से भागने तक, उनका जीवन लगातार खतरे में था।
teaching_local: राज्य जनता की सुरक्षा और समृद्धि के लिए बनाया जाता है।
moral_local: दृष्टिकोण, रणनीतिक कौशल और नैतिक सत्यनिष्ठा द्वारा समर्थित होकर, पहाड़ों को भी हिला सकता है।

name: Bhakta Dhruv
tagline: The five-year-old child whose fierce determination immortalized him as the North Star.
journey: Insulted by his stepmother and denied a place on his father's lap, young Dhruv went into the forest to seek Lord Vishnu. With a willpower that shook the heavens, he meditated until Vishnu granted him the highest, unmoving seat in the cosmos.
trial: A child surviving alone in a dark, beast-filled forest, fueled only by an iron resolve to find God.
teaching: Determination directed toward the divine never fails.
moral: No one is too young to achieve the highest spiritual heights.
journey_local: सौतेली माँ द्वारा अपमानित, युवा ध्रुव भगवान विष्णु की खोज में जंगल में चला गया और ध्यान किया।
trial_local: एक बच्चा जो केवल भगवान को खोजने के दृढ़ संकल्प से प्रेरित होकर अकेले जंगल में जीवित रहा।
teaching_local: ईश्वर की ओर निर्देशित संकल्प कभी विफल नहीं होता।
moral_local: कोई भी व्यक्ति उच्चतम आध्यात्मिक ऊंचाइयों को प्राप्त करने के लिए बहुत छोटा नहीं है।

name: Eknath
tagline: Eknath was a medieval Hindu saint whose life exemplified devotion, service, and equality through his spiritual teachings and actions.
journey: Eknath lived during the medieval era in India, a period marked by deep spiritual exploration. His life was dedicated to the path of bhakti, or devotion, which he pursued with unwavering commitment. He became a revered figure, known for his spiritual wisdom and compassionate nature. His journey was not just personal but also influential, touching the lives of many who sought guidance and solace in his teachings. He navigated the complexities of his time with grace, embodying the principles of service and equality.
trial: Eknath faced the spiritual trials inherent in a life of deep devotion. His path was one of constant self-reflection and service, requiring him to transcend societal norms and personal ego. He navigated the challenges of his era with a spirit of equality, ensuring his teachings were accessible to all. His sacrifice was in dedicating his life entirely to the divine and to the upliftment of others, a testament to his profound spiritual commitment.
teaching: Eknath's core contribution was his unwavering dedication to bhakti, the path of devotion. He taught that true spirituality lies in selfless service and seeing the divine in all beings, embodying the principle of equality. His teachings emphasized a personal, loving connection with the divine, accessible to everyone regardless of social standing. He was a beacon of spiritual wisdom, guiding others through the power of devotion and compassion.
moral: A modern seeker can learn from Eknath the importance of unwavering devotion and selfless service. His life teaches that true spirituality transcends social barriers and is rooted in compassion and equality. By dedicating oneself to a higher purpose and serving others without expectation, one can find profound spiritual fulfillment and make a positive impact on the world.
legacy: Eknath's life shaped the tradition of bhakti in India, leaving a lasting legacy of devotion and equality. He inspired countless individuals to pursue a path of selfless service and love for the divine. His teachings continue to resonate, influencing spiritual thought and practice. He stands as a testament to the power of a life lived in service and devotion, enriching the cultural and spiritual fabric of his time.
journey_local: एकनाथ मध्यकालीन भारत में एक संत थे जिनका जीवन भक्ति, सेवा और समानता के सिद्धांतों को दर्शाता था।
trial_local: एकनाथ ने भक्ति के मार्ग पर गहरी आध्यात्मिक चुनौतियों का सामना किया।
teaching_local: एकनाथ का मुख्य योगदान भक्ति मार्ग के प्रति उनकी अटूट निष्ठा थी।
moral_local: एक आधुनिक साधक एकनाथ से अटूट भक्ति और निस्वार्थ सेवा का महत्व सीख सकता है।
legacy_local: एकनाथ के जीवन ने भारत में भक्ति परंपरा को आकार दिया, भक्ति और समानता की स्थायी विरासत छोड़ी।

name: Emperor Ashoka
tagline: The fierce conqueror who laid down his sword after seeing the cost of war, transforming into the greatest patron of Dhamma.
journey:
Ashoka began his rule as 'Chandashoka' (Ashoka the Fierce), violently expanding the Mauryan Empire. The climax of his conquests was the Kalinga War, which resulted in the deaths of over 100,000 people. Walking through the blood-soaked battlefield, listening to the wails of orphans and widows, Ashoka experienced a profound existential crisis and overwhelming remorse.

He renounced violence, embraced Buddhism, and became 'Dharmashoka' (Ashoka the Pious). He replaced the drum of war (Bheri-ghosha) with the drum of righteousness (Dhamma-ghosha). He carved edicts on rocks and pillars across his vast empire, promoting religious tolerance, animal welfare, medical care for all, and moral conduct. He sent emissaries, including his own children, to spread the Buddha's peaceful message across Asia.
trial: His trial was the transformation of his own nature. Having built his identity on unmatched power and terror, it took immense courage for the most powerful emperor on earth to publicly admit his horrific mistakes, apologize to his subjects via stone edicts, and fundamentally change the mechanics of an empire from conquest to compassion.
teaching: All men are my children. Just as I desire for my children that they may obtain every kind of welfare and happiness, so do I desire for all men.
moral: True power is not measured by the lands you conquer, but by the hearts you heal.
quote: There is no gift like the gift of Dhamma.
journey_local: अशोक ने 'चंडाशोक' के रूप में शुरुआत की। कलिंग युद्ध में एक लाख से अधिक लोगों की मौत के बाद, खून से सने युद्ध के मैदान में उन्हें गहरा पश्चाताप हुआ। उन्होंने हिंसा त्याग दी, बौद्ध धर्म अपनाया और 'धर्माशोक' बन गए। उन्होंने युद्ध के ढोल को धम्म के ढोल से बदल दिया और पूरे एशिया में बुद्ध के शांतिपूर्ण संदेश का प्रसार किया।
trial_local: उनकी परीक्षा अपने स्वयं के स्वभाव का परिवर्तन था। धरती के सबसे शक्तिशाली सम्राट के लिए अपनी भयानक गलतियों को सार्वजनिक रूप से स्वीकार करना, अपने विषयों से माफी मांगना और साम्राज्य को विजय से करुणा में बदलना बहुत साहस का काम था।
teaching_local: सभी मनुष्य मेरे बच्चे हैं। जिस प्रकार मैं अपने बच्चों के कल्याण और सुख की कामना करता हूँ, उसी प्रकार मैं सभी मनुष्यों के लिए कामना करता हूँ।
moral_local: सच्ची शक्ति इस बात से नहीं मापी जाती कि आप कितने राज्यों को जीतते हैं, बल्कि इससे कि आप कितने दिलों को ठीक करते हैं।
quote_local: धम्म के दान के समान कोई दान नहीं है।

name: Gautama Swami (Indrabhuti)
tagline: The proud Brahmin scholar whose ego melted at the feet of Lord Mahavira.
journey: Indrabhuti Gautama was the most famous and proud Vedic scholar of his time. He went to confront Mahavira, intending to defeat him in debate. However, Mahavira welcomed him by his secret name and answered all the unasked doubts in Gautama's mind regarding the nature of the soul. Deeply moved, Gautama surrendered his immense pride and became Mahavira's chief disciple (Ganadhara).
trial: Despite his vast knowledge, his deep personal attachment and love for Mahavira prevented him from attaining omniscience while Mahavira was alive. He had to learn to detach even from his beloved Guru.
teaching: True knowledge requires the complete surrender of intellectual pride.
moral: Even the holiest attachments can bind the soul; ultimate liberation requires letting go of everything.
journey_local: इंद्रभूति गौतम अपने समय के सबसे प्रसिद्ध और गर्वित वैदिक विद्वान थे। महावीर से मिलने पर उनका अहंकार दूर हो गया और वे उनके मुख्य शिष्य बन गए।
trial_local: उनके विशाल ज्ञान के बावजूद, महावीर के प्रति उनके गहरे व्यक्तिगत लगाव ने उन्हें महावीर के जीवित रहते केवल ज्ञान प्राप्त करने से रोक दिया।
teaching_local: सच्चे ज्ञान के लिए बौद्धिक अभिमान के पूर्ण आत्मसमर्पण की आवश्यकता होती है।
moral_local: यहां तक कि सबसे पवित्र जुड़ाव भी आत्मा को बांध सकते हैं; अंतिम मुक्ति के लिए सब कुछ छोड़ने की आवश्यकता होती है।

name: Guru Arjan Dev Ji
tagline: The fifth Guru who compiled the Adi Granth and became the first Sikh martyr.
journey: Guru Arjan Dev Ji consolidated the Sikh faith by compiling the hymns of the previous Gurus and other saints (including Hindu and Sufi mystics) into the Adi Granth. He also built the Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) with four doors, welcoming people from all directions and castes. His growing influence alarmed the Mughal Emperor Jahangir.
trial: Arrested on false charges, he was subjected to excruciating torture—made to sit on a burning iron plate while hot sand was poured over him. Through days of agony, he remained in deep meditation, repeating "Tera kiya meetha laage" (Your will is sweet to me).
teaching: Tera kiya meetha laage, Har naam padarath Nanak maange.
moral: Absolute surrender to the Divine will is the highest form of spiritual strength.
journey_local: ਗੁਰੂ ਅਰਜਨ ਦੇਵ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਪਿਛਲੇ ਗੁਰੂਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਹੋਰ ਸੰਤਾਂ ਦੀ ਬਾਣੀ ਨੂੰ ਆਦਿ ਗ੍ਰੰਥ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੰਕਲਿਤ ਕੀਤਾ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਹਰਿਮੰਦਰ ਸਾਹਿਬ ਬਣਵਾਇਆ।
trial_local: ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਤੱਤੀ ਤਵੀ 'ਤੇ ਬਿਠਾਇਆ ਗਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਗਰਮ ਰੇਤ ਪਾਈ ਗਈ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਸ਼ਾਂਤੀ ਨਾਲ "ਤੇਰਾ ਕੀਆ ਮੀਠਾ ਲਾਗੈ" ਦਾ ਜਾਪ ਕੀਤਾ।
teaching_local: ਤੇਰਾ ਕੀਆ ਮੀਠਾ ਲਾਗੈ॥ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਪਦਾਰਥੁ ਨਾਨਕੁ ਮਾਂਗੈ॥
moral_local: ਪ੍ਰਮਾਤਮਾ ਦੀ ਰਜ਼ਾ ਵਿੱਚ ਪੂਰਨ ਸਮਰਪਣ ਅਧਿਆਤਮਿਕ ਸ਼ਕਤੀ ਦਾ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਚਾ ਰੂप ਹੈ।

name: Guru Gobind Singh Ji
tagline: The poet-warrior who transformed saints into soldiers, creating the Khalsa to protect righteousness.
journey:
Becoming the tenth Guru at the tender age of nine after his father, Guru Tegh Bahadur, was martyred, Gobind Rai knew that passive resistance was no longer enough. He was a master of martial arts, a scholar of multiple languages, and a prolific poet.

On Vaisakhi in 1699, he forged the Khalsa, an order of saint-soldiers. He asked for five heads in sacrifice, and the 'Panj Pyare' who stepped forward were given amrit and the surname 'Singh' (Lion). In a historic act of humility, the Guru then knelt and asked them to initiate him into the Khalsa.
trial: His trials were unimaginably severe. He fought endless defensive wars, lost all four of his sons, and his mother. Yet, through this devastating personal loss, he wrote the 'Zafarnama' to Emperor Aurangzeb, declaring that moral victory belonged to the Khalsa.
teaching: When all peaceful means to resolve a conflict fail, it is righteous to draw the sword.
moral: Courage is fighting for justice even when you have lost everything.
journey_local: ਨੌਂ ਸਾਲ ਦੀ ਉਮਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਦਸਵੇਂ ਗੁਰੂ ਬਣੇ, ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੇ ਦੇਖਿਆ ਕਿ ਹੁਣ ਸਿਰਫ਼ ਸ਼ਾਂਤਮਈ ਵਿਰੋਧ ਕਾਫ਼ੀ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ। ੧੬੯੯ ਦੀ ਵਿਸਾਖੀ ਵਾਲੇ ਦਿਨ, ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੇ ਸੰਤ-ਸਿਪਾਹੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਖਾਲਸਾ ਪੰਥ ਦੀ ਸਾਜਨਾ ਕੀਤੀ।
trial_local: ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਪ੍ਰੀਖਿਆਵਾਂ ਬਹੁਤ ਕਠਿਨ ਸਨ। ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੇ ਮੁਗਲ ਸਾਮਰਾਜ ਵਿਰੁੱਧ ਕਈ ਜੰਗਾਂ ਲੜੀਆਂ। ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਚਾਰੇ ਪੁੱਤਰਾਂ ਅਤੇ ਮਾਤਾ ਜੀ ਨੂੰ ਗਵਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ। ਫਿਰ ਵੀ, ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੇ ਔਰੰਗਜ਼ੇਬ ਨੂੰ 'ਜ਼ਫ਼ਰਨਾਮਾ' ਲਿਖਿਆ।
teaching_local: ਚੂੰ ਕਾਰ ਅਜ਼ ਹਮਹ ਹੀਲਤੇ ਦਰ ਗੁਜ਼ਸ਼ਤ॥ ਹਲਾਲ ਅਸਤ ਬੁਰਦਨ ਬ-ਸ਼ਮਸ਼ੀਰ ਦਸਤ॥
moral_local: ਦਲੇਰੀ ਉਦੋਂ ਵੀ ਇਨਸਾਫ਼ ਲਈ ਲੜਨਾ ਹੈ ਜਦੋਂ ਤੁਸੀਂ ਸਭ ਕੁਝ ਗੁਆ ਚੁੱਕੇ ਹੋਵੋ।

name: Guru Nanak Dev Ji
tagline: The founding Guru who walked thousands of miles to sing of the One Divine and tear down the walls of caste and ritual.
journey:
Born in Talwandi, Nanak showed a deep spiritual inclination from childhood. After a profound mystical experience at the river Bein, he emerged with a simple but revolutionary message: "There is no Hindu, there is no Musalman" — meaning that in the eyes of the Divine, all artificial human divisions are meaningless.

He spent the next 24 years undertaking four massive journeys (Udasis) on foot, traveling as far as Tibet, Mecca, and Sri Lanka. Accompanied by his Muslim companion Bhai Mardana, he used divine poetry (Kirtan) to gently dismantle hypocrisy, blind rituals, and caste oppression. He settled in Kartarpur, where he instituted 'Langar' (community kitchen) where kings and beggars sat on the same floor to eat together.
trial: His trial was confronting the rigid, powerful religious establishments of his time. He faced anger, ridicule, and threats from both orthodox Hindu priests and conservative Islamic clerics. Yet, he never used anger or violence; his weapon was always profound logic wrapped in divine love and humility.
teaching: Kirat Karo, Naam Japo, Vand Chhako (Earn an honest living, remember the Divine, and share with others).
moral: True spirituality is not escaping the world, but living truthfully and compassionately within it.
journey_local: ਤਲਵੰਡੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਜਨਮੇ, ਨਾਨਕ ਦਾ ਬਚਪਨ ਤੋਂ ਹੀ ਅਧਿਆਤਮਿਕ ਝੁਕਾਅ ਸੀ। ਵੇਈਂ ਨਦੀ 'ਤੇ ਇੱਕ ਡੂੰਘੇ ਅਨੁਭਵ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ, ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੇ ਇੱਕ ਕ੍ਰਾਂਤੀਕਾਰੀ ਸੰਦੇਸ਼ ਦਿੱਤਾ: "ਨਾ ਕੋਈ ਹਿੰਦੂ, ਨਾ ਕੋਈ ਮੁਸਲਮਾਨ"। ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੇ ਤਿੱਬਤ, ਮੱਕਾ ਅਤੇ ਸ੍ਰੀ ਲੰਕਾ ਤੱਕ ਦੀਆਂ ਚਾਰ ਵੱਡੀਆਂ ਉਦਾਸੀਆਂ ਕੀਤੀਆਂ।
trial_local: ਉਹਨਾਂ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰੀਖਿਆ ਆਪਣੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਦੀਆਂ ਕੱਟੜ ਧਾਰਮਿਕ ਸੰਸਥਾਵਾਂ ਦਾ ਸਾਹਮਣਾ ਕਰਨਾ ਸੀ। ਉਹਨਾਂ ਨੇ ਪੁਜਾਰੀਆਂ ਅਤੇ ਮੌਲਵੀਆਂ ਦੇ ਗੁੱਸੇ ਦਾ ਸਾਹਮਣਾ ਕੀਤਾ, ਪਰ ਕਦੇ ਗੁੱਸੇ ਜਾਂ ਹਿੰਸਾ ਦੀ ਵਰਤੋਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਕੀਤੀ।
teaching_local: ਕਿਰਤ ਕਰੋ, ਨਾਮ ਜਪੋ, ਵੰਡ ਛਕੋ।
moral_local: ਸੱਚਾ ਅਧਿਆਤਮਵਾਦ ਦੁਨੀਆ ਤੋਂ ਭੱਜਣਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਹੈ, ਸਗੋਂ ਇਸ ਵਿੱਚ ਸੱਚਾਈ ਅਤੇ ਹਮਦਰਦੀ ਨਾਲ ਜੀਣਾ ਹੈ।

name: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji
tagline: The Shield of India who sacrificed his life to protect the religious freedom of another faith.
journey: A quiet, meditative man who spent years in contemplation before assuming Guruship. When a delegation of Kashmiri Pandits, facing forced conversion under Emperor Aurangzeb, pleaded for help, the Guru stepped forward. He told Aurangzeb that if he could convert the Guru, all Hindus would follow. Thus, he knowingly placed himself in the path of execution to save others.
trial: Imprisoned in Delhi in an iron cage, he was forced to watch his closest disciples sawn in half and boiled alive to break his resolve. He refused to convert or perform miracles, choosing to be publicly beheaded at Chandni Chowk to uphold the universal right to freedom of conscience.
teaching: Fear none, and strike fear in none.
moral: True dharma is protecting the rights of others, even those whose beliefs differ from your own.
journey_local: ਜਦੋਂ ਕਸ਼ਮੀਰੀ ਪੰਡਤਾਂ ਨੇ ਔਰੰਗਜ਼ੇਬ ਦੇ ਜ਼ੁਲਮ ਤੋਂ ਬਚਣ ਲਈ ਮਦਦ ਮੰਗੀ, ਤਾਂ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਰੱਖਿਆ ਲਈ ਆਪਣੀ ਜਾਨ ਦੇ ਦਿੱਤੀ।
trial_local: ਦਿੱਲੀ ਵਿੱਚ ਕੈਦ, ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਆਪਣੇ ਸਾਥੀਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਸ਼ਹੀਦ ਹੁੰਦੇ ਦੇਖਿਆ ਪਰ ਆਪਣਾ ਇਰਾਦਾ ਨਹੀਂ ਬਦਲਿਆ।
teaching_local: ਭੈ ਕਾਹੂ ਕਉ ਦੇਤ ਨਹਿ ਨਹਿ ਭੈ ਮਾਨਤ ਆਨ॥
moral_local: ਸੱਚਾ ਧਰਮ ਦੂਜਿਆਂ ਦੇ ਹੱਕਾਂ ਦੀ ਰਾਖੀ ਕਰਨਾ ਹੈ, ਭਾਵੇਂ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਵਿਸ਼ਵਾਸ ਤੁਹਾਡੇ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਖਰੇ ਹੋਣ।

name: Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji
tagline: Deep spiritual dedication transcending boundaries of faith and sacrifice in turbulent times, guided by inner wisdom and courage
journey: According to the sources, Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji lived during a period filled with religious and political turmoil. The texts mention that times were challenging, with references to events like the 1857 mutiny and Kuka outbreaks. While specific details about his journey are limited in the provided passages, the sources indicate that he was connected to important prophetic traditions within the Sikh faith. He maintained connections through key figures who would later interact with his spiritual legacy.
trial: The sources heavily focus on broader historical upheavals rather than detailing Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji's specific trials. The texts mention religious disturbances and the 1857 mutiny, which may reflect challenging times for spiritual figures of that era. The Kuka movement is also referenced as part of the religious landscape. While martyrdom is implied as a theme, the sources do not provide concrete details of his personal trials and sacrifices.
teaching: The sources emphasize profound spiritual teachings about attaining divine connection through inner realization. Key teachings include living entirely in God or not living at all, knowing oneself completely, and seeing through God's eyes to achieve true wisdom. The texts stress that external practices without inner realization are empty, and that one must become a living temple of God. Spiritual awakening is presented as essential for understanding the eternal reality.
moral: Modern seekers cultivate authentic spiritual understanding beyond external rituals and dogmatic obedience. By emphasizing inner realization and direct connection with the divine, individuals develop authentic character based on truth. The sources advocate against zealous hatred of other beliefs while maintaining deep spiritual commitment rooted in personal experience rather than blind imitation.
legacy: The sources reflect on significant transformations within the Sikh tradition, particularly regarding prophetic interpretations and social structures. The texts discuss how prophecies were sometimes modified to suit contemporary needs, suggesting an evolving spiritual understanding. The mention of low caste rising to power indicates social dynamics within the tradition. The Kuka movement's emergence illustrates how spiritual interpretations influenced religious and political landscapes.
quote: Live in God or do not live at all.
journey_local: स्रोतों के अनुसार, गुरु तेग बहादुर जी का जीवन धार्मिक और राजनीतिक उथल-पुथल के काल में बीता। 1857 के विद्रोह और कुका उठावन जैसी घटनाओं का संदर्भ दिया गया है। यहाँ उनके जीवन के विशिष्ट विवरण सीमित हैं, लेकिन वे सिख परंपरा के भीतर महत्वपूर्ण भविष्यवाणियों से जुड़े हुए थे।
trial_local: स्रोत गुरु तेग बहादुर जी की विशिष्ट परीक्षाओं के बारे में अधिक केंद्रित नहीं हैं। 1857 के विद्रोह और धार्मिक उथल-पुथल का उल्लेख किया गया है, जो उस समय के आध्यात्मिक हस्तियों के लिए कठिनाइयों को दर्शाता है।
teaching_local: स्रोत परम दिव्य संबंध प्राप्त करने के लिए आंतरिक अनुभूति पर केंद्रित गहरे आध्यात्मिक शिक्षाओं पर जोर देते हैं। प्रमुख शिक्षाओं में हैं- पूरी तरह से ईश्वर में रहना या न रहना, अपने को पूरी तरह जानना, और ईश्वर की आँखों से देखना।
moral_local: आधुनिक साधक बाहरी कर्मकांडों और अंध हुकुमों से परे वास्तविक आध्यात्मिक समझ विकसित करते हैं। सत्य पर आधारित प्रामाणिक चरित्र को बढ़ावा देते हुए, आंतरिक अनुभूति को महत्व देते हैं।
legacy_local: स्रोत सिख परंपरा के भीतर महत्वपूर्ण परिवर्तनों पर विचार करते हैं। भविष्यवाणियों की व्याख्या और सामाजिक संरचनाओं में बदलाव का उल्लेख किया गया है।
quote_local: ईश्वर में रहो या जीओ मत।

name: Sri Hanuman
tagline: The supreme devotee whose immense power was unlocked only by his absolute surrender to Rama.
journey: Minister of the Vanara king Sugriva, Hanuman crossed the ocean in a single leap to find Mother Sita. He burned down Lanka, brought the Sanjeevani mountain to save Lakshmana, and tore open his chest to show that Rama and Sita lived within his heart.
trial: He possessed god-like strength but was cursed to forget it. He could only remember his power when reminded of his purpose—serving the Divine.
teaching: Dasanudaso Aham (I am the servant of the servant of God).
moral: Infinite power flows through you when you have zero ego and perfect devotion.
journey_local: वानर राजा सुग्रीव के मंत्री, हनुमान ने एक छलांग में समुद्र पार किया और लंका को जला दिया।
trial_local: उनके पास देवता जैसी शक्ति थी लेकिन उन्हें इसे भूलने का श्राप मिला था।
teaching_local: मैं भगवान के सेवक का सेवक हूँ।
moral_local: जब आपके पास शून्य अहंकार और पूर्ण भक्ति होती है तो आपके माध्यम से अनंत शक्ति बहती है।

name: Hari Singh Nalwa
tagline: The legendary commander who reversed centuries of invasions and struck terror in the Khyber Pass.
journey: Commander-in-chief of the Sikh Khalsa Army under Maharaja Ranjit Singh. For centuries, India had been invaded through the Afghan passes. Nalwa reversed this trend entirely. He conquered Kasur, Multan, Attock, Peshawar, and Jamrud, expanding the Sikh Empire to the very mouth of the Khyber Pass.
trial: His trial was fighting a brutal, relentless mountain war against hardened Afghan tribes. Even after being mortally wounded at the Battle of Jamrud, he ordered his troops not to announce his death until reinforcements arrived, keeping the enemy at bay with just the terror of his name.
teaching: Offense is the best defense of the homeland.
moral: A singular, disciplined will can reverse the tide of history.
journey_local: ਮਹਾਰਾਜਾ ਰਣਜੀਤ ਸਿੰਘ ਦੇ ਅਧੀਨ ਸਿੱਖ ਖਾਲਸਾ ਫੌਜ ਦੇ ਕਮਾਂਡਰ-ਇਨ-ਚੀਫ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਅਫਗਾਨਿਸਤਾਨ ਵੱਲੋਂ ਹੁੰਦੇ ਹਮਲਿਆਂ ਨੂੰ ਰੋਕਿਆ ਅਤੇ ਸਿੱਖ ਸਾਮਰਾਜ ਦਾ ਵਿਸਥਾਰ ਕੀਤਾ।
trial_local: ਜਮਰੌਦ ਦੀ ਲੜਾਈ ਵਿੱਚ ਬੁਰੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਜ਼ਖਮੀ ਹੋਣ ਤੋਂ ਬਾਅਦ ਵੀ, ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਹੁਕਮ ਦਿੱਤਾ ਕਿ ਮਦਦ ਪਹੁੰਚਣ ਤੱਕ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਮੌਤ ਦੀ ਖ਼ਬਰ ਨਾ ਦਿੱਤੀ ਜਾਵੇ।
teaching_local: ਹਮਲਾ ਹੀ ਮਾਤਭੂਮੀ ਦਾ ਸਭ ਤੋਂ ਵਧੀਆ ਬਚਾਅ ਹੈ।
moral_local: ਇੱਕ ਅਨੁਸ਼ਾਸਿਤ ਇੱਛਾ-ਸ਼ਕਤੀ ਇਤਿਹਾਸ ਦਾ ਰੁਖ ਮੋੜ ਸਕਦੀ ਹੈ।

name: Haribhadra Suri
tagline: The brilliant Brahmin who synthesized Indian philosophy through the lens of Jain Anekantavada.
journey: A proud Vedic scholar who boasted he would become the disciple of anyone who could present a text he couldn't understand. He was stumped by a verse sung by a Jain nun, Yakini Mahattara. True to his word, he converted to Jainism. He authored over 1,400 texts, remarkably showing deep respect for Buddhist and Hindu philosophies, synthesizing them under the Jain doctrine of multiple viewpoints (Anekantavada).
trial: His trial was overcoming severe anger. When his two nephews were killed by rival Buddhist monks, he plotted a violent magical revenge. His Guru stopped him, making him realize that anger destroys one's own soul first.
teaching: I have no bias for Mahavira, and no hatred for Kapila or others. Whosoever speaks the truth is my teacher.
moral: Truth is multi-faceted; open-mindedness is the hallmark of true spiritual maturity.
journey_local: एक गर्वित वैदिक विद्वान जो एक जैन नन द्वारा गाए गए एक श्लोक से चकित रह गया। उन्होंने जैन धर्म अपना लिया और 1,400 से अधिक ग्रंथों की रचना की।
trial_local: उनका परीक्षण गंभीर क्रोध पर काबू पाना था। जब उनके दो भतीजों को प्रतिद्वंद्वी बौद्ध भिक्षुओं ने मार डाला, तो उन्होंने हिंसक बदला लेने की साजिश रची।
teaching_local: मुझे महावीर के लिए कोई पक्षपात नहीं है, और दूसरों के लिए कोई नफरत नहीं है। जो कोई भी सत्य बोलता है वह मेरा शिक्षक है।
moral_local: सत्य बहुआयामी है; खुले विचारों वाला होना सच्ची आध्यात्मिक परिपक्वता की पहचान है।

name: King Harishchandra
tagline: The king who lost his kingdom, wife, and son, but refused to utter a single lie.
journey: To honor a promise made to Sage Vishwamitra in a dream, he gave away his entire kingdom. Left penniless, he sold his wife, his son, and himself into slavery. Working as a corpse-burner in a crematorium, he maintained his vow of truth.
trial: When his own wife brought their dead son's body to the cremation ground, he refused to cremate the boy without the requisite tax, upholding his duty to his master over his own grief.
teaching: Satyamev Jayate (Truth alone triumphs).
moral: Truth is an absolute value; it is not subject to convenience or circumstance.
journey_local: सपने में किए गए वादे का सम्मान करने के लिए, उन्होंने अपना पूरा राज्य दे दिया।
trial_local: जब उनकी पत्नी उनके मृत बेटे का शव लेकर आई, तो उन्होंने कर लिए बिना उसका अंतिम संस्कार करने से इनकार कर दिया।
teaching_local: सत्यमेव जयते।
moral_local: सत्य एक पूर्ण मूल्य है; यह सुविधा या परिस्थिति के अधीन नहीं है।

name: Acharya Hemachandra
tagline: The polymath "Omniscient of the Kali Age" who transformed a kingdom through literature and ethics.
journey: A prodigious monk, Hemachandra mastered logic, grammar, poetry, and philosophy. He became the spiritual advisor to King Kumarpal of Gujarat. Instead of seeking power, he guided the king to turn his state into a model of Jain ethics—banning animal slaughter, promoting vegetarianism, and building libraries.
trial: His trial was existing at the heights of royal power without being corrupted by it, using his vast intellect solely as a tool to alleviate the suffering of humans and animals across the kingdom.
teaching: Knowledge is a weapon to cut through the darkness of ignorance, not an ornament to decorate the ego.
moral: Intellect and political influence must always be guided by absolute compassion.
journey_local: एक विलक्षण भिक्षु, हेमचंद्र ने तर्क, व्याकरण, कविता और दर्शन में महारत हासिल की। वे गुजरात के राजा कुमारपाल के आध्यात्मिक सलाहकार बने।
trial_local: उनका परीक्षण शाही शक्ति की ऊंचाइयों पर मौजूद होना था, बिना इसके भ्रष्ट हुए।
teaching_local: ज्ञान अज्ञान के अंधकार को काटने का हथियार है, अहंकार को सजाने का आभूषण नहीं।
moral_local: बुद्धि और राजनीतिक प्रभाव को हमेशा पूर्ण करुणा द्वारा निर्देशित किया जाना चाहिए।

name: Sant Kabir Das
tagline: The mystic weaver who ripped away the veil of religious hypocrisy with his sharp couplets.
journey: Raised in a Muslim weaver family, Kabir became a disciple of the Hindu saint Ramananda. He rejected the dogma of both religions, experiencing the Divine as Nirguna (formless). His raw, blunt Doha (couplets) struck directly at the heart of ego and ritualism.
trial: Persecuted by both Hindu and Muslim orthodoxy for declaring that God resides neither in the temple nor the mosque, but in the heart.
teaching: Moko kahan dhunde re bande, main to tere paas mein.
moral: The divine is within you; all external searching is an illusion.
journey_local: एक मुस्लिम जुलाहा परिवार में पले-बढ़े कबीर हिंदू संत रामानंद के शिष्य बने।
trial_local: यह घोषित करने के लिए कि भगवान मंदिर या मस्जिद में नहीं, बल्कि हृदय में निवास करते हैं, उन्हें सताया गया।
teaching_local: मोको कहाँ ढूँढे रे बंदे, मैं तो तेरे पास में।
moral_local: ईश्वर आपके भीतर है; सभी बाहरी खोज एक भ्रम है।

name: King Kumarpal
tagline: The Solanki Emperor who transformed a vast empire into a sanctuary of non-violence.
journey: Kumarpal spent years as a fugitive before claiming the throne of Gujarat. Under the guidance of Acharya Hemachandra, he underwent a profound personal transformation. He enforced strict laws against animal slaughter, hunting, gambling, and alcohol across his vast empire, essentially running a state based on Jain ethical principles without dismantling its administrative strength.
trial: His trial was balancing the ruthless demands of medieval statecraft and military defense with the absolute vows of non-violence, maintaining order while radically reforming society.
teaching: A true king protects the weakest creature in his kingdom with the same zeal he protects his borders.
moral: Political power is best used to create an environment where compassion and ethics can flourish.
journey_local: कुमारपाल ने गुजरात के सिंहासन का दावा करने से पहले वर्षों तक एक भगोड़े के रूप में बिताया। आचार्य हेमचंद्र के मार्गदर्शन में, उन्होंने एक गहरा व्यक्तिगत परिवर्तन किया।
trial_local: उनका परीक्षण मध्ययुगीन शासन और सैन्य रक्षा की क्रूर मांगों को अहिंसा के पूर्ण व्रतों के साथ संतुलित करना था।
teaching_local: एक सच्चा राजा अपने राज्य के सबसे कमजोर प्राणी की रक्षा उसी उत्साह के साथ करता है जिससे वह अपनी सीमाओं की रक्षा करता है।
moral_local: राजनीतिक शक्ति का सबसे अच्छा उपयोग एक ऐसा वातावरण बनाने के लिए किया जाता है जहां करुणा और नैतिकता पनप सकें।

name: Acharya Kundakunda
tagline: The mystic-scholar whose verses defined the essence of Jain soul-philosophy.
journey: Kundakunda is one of the most revered figures in Jainism. He authored foundational texts like the Samayasara and Pravachanasara. He boldly distinguished between the practical standpoint (vyavahara naya) of rituals and the ultimate standpoint (nishchaya naya) of the pure soul, re-centering Jainism on internal realization rather than just external austerity.
trial: He had to navigate a time when external rituals were overshadowing inner spiritual work, writing uncompromising philosophy that stripped away all illusions of the material world.
teaching: The soul alone is my true nature; all other things are foreign to me.
moral: External actions only matter if they lead to internal purification.
journey_local: कुंदकुंद जैन धर्म में सबसे पूजनीय हस्तियों में से एक हैं। उन्होंने समयसार और प्रवचनसार जैसे ग्रंथों की रचना की।
trial_local: उन्हें ऐसे समय को नेविगेट करना पड़ा जब बाहरी अनुष्ठान आंतरिक आध्यात्मिक कार्यों पर हावी हो रहे थे।
teaching_local: केवल आत्मा ही मेरा वास्तविक स्वरूप है; अन्य सभी चीजें मेरे लिए विदेशी हैं।
moral_local: बाहरी कार्य तभी मायने रखते हैं जब वे आंतरिक शुद्धि की ओर ले जाते हैं।

name: Lonka Saha
tagline: The scribe who read the original texts and sparked a massive reform movement.
journey: Employed by monks to copy ancient Jain manuscripts, Lonka Saha, a layman, actually read the texts he was copying. He realized that the lavish temple building and idol-worship practices of his time were not mentioned in the original Agamas. Courageously, he stood up against powerful clerical authorities and advocated for a return to pure, internal spiritual practice, founding the Sthanakvasi tradition.
trial: He faced immense backlash, excommunication, and hatred from the religious establishment for daring to challenge centuries of entrenched institutional practices using the religion's own texts.
teaching: Truth is found in the scriptures and the heart, not in stone or rituals.
moral: Never blindly accept tradition; seek the truth at its source with an open mind.
journey_local: प्राचीन जैन पांडुलिपियों की नकल करने के लिए भिक्षुओं द्वारा नियोजित, लोंका शाह ने वास्तव में उन ग्रंथों को पढ़ा जिनकी वह नकल कर रहे थे।
trial_local: उन्हें धार्मिक प्रतिष्ठान से भारी प्रतिक्रिया और नफरत का सामना करना पड़ा।
teaching_local: सत्य शास्त्रों और हृदय में पाया जाता है, पत्थर या अनुष्ठानों में नहीं।
moral_local: परंपरा को कभी भी आंख मूंदकर स्वीकार न करें; खुले दिमाग से सत्य को उसके स्रोत पर खोजें।

name: Lord Mahavira
tagline: The 24th Tirthankara who conquered his own inner enemies to teach the world the supreme path of Ahimsa.
journey:
Born as Prince Vardhamana into royal luxury, he realized early that true happiness cannot be found in material power. At age 30, he renounced his kingdom, his family, and even his clothes, embarking on a severe path of asceticism. For twelve and a half years, he wandered in deep meditation, enduring extreme weather, fasting, and physical attacks from ignorant people, yet he never retaliated or felt anger.

At the age of 42, he attained Kevala Jnana (omniscience). He then spent the next 30 years walking barefoot across India, preaching the principles of Ahimsa (non-violence), Anekantavada (multi-sidedness of truth), and Aparigraha (non-attachment). He reformed society by opposing animal sacrifice and the caste system, establishing a four-fold order of monks, nuns, and laypeople.
trial: His trial was absolute endurance. Once, a cowherd drove nails into Mahavira's ears while he was in deep meditation, but Mahavira felt only compassion for the man's ignorance. His true conquest was not over external lands, but over the internal enemies of anger, ego, deceit, and greed.
teaching: Ahimsa Paramo Dharma. Non-violence is the highest religion.
moral: The greatest victory is not conquering millions in battle, but conquering your own mind.
journey_local: राजकुमार वर्धमान के रूप में जन्मे, उन्होंने ३० वर्ष की आयु में अपना राज्य त्याग दिया। साढ़े बारह वर्षों तक, उन्होंने कठोर तपस्या और ध्यान किया। ४२ वर्ष की आयु में उन्हें केवल ज्ञान प्राप्त हुआ। अगले ३० वर्षों तक उन्होंने पूरे भारत में यात्रा की और अहिंसा, अनेकांतवाद और अपरिग्रह का उपदेश दिया।
trial_local: उनकी परीक्षा पूर्ण सहनशीलता थी। एक बार ध्यान के दौरान एक चरवाहे ने उनके कानों में कीलें ठोक दीं, लेकिन महावीर ने केवल करुणा महसूस की।
teaching_local: अहिंसा परमो धर्मः। अहिंसा ही सर्वोच्च धर्म है।
moral_local: सबसे बड़ी जीत युद्ध में लाखों को जीतना नहीं है, बल्कि अपने स्वयं के मन को जीतना है।

name: Mahapajapati Gotami
tagline: The foster mother of the Buddha who led the first order of Buddhist nuns.
journey: After the death of Queen Maya, Mahapajapati raised Siddhartha as her own son. Following the death of her husband, King Suddhodana, she led a large group of Sakyan women on a grueling barefoot march to request the Buddha to allow women to ordain as monastics. After initial refusal, she persisted until the Buddha established the Bhikkhuni Sangha.
trial: She faced the immense societal patriarchy of her time, enduring a long, painful physical journey covered in dust and with swollen feet, just to prove that women were equally capable of attaining spiritual liberation.
teaching: Women are just as capable as men of reaching the highest states of awakening.
moral: Perseverance in the face of systemic barriers opens doors not just for oneself, but for generations.
journey_local: रानी माया की मृत्यु के बाद, महाप्रजापति ने सिद्धार्थ को अपने पुत्र के रूप में पाला। उन्होंने शाक्य महिलाओं के एक समूह का नेतृत्व कर बुद्ध से महिलाओं को संन्यास लेने की अनुमति मांगी।
trial_local: उन्होंने अपने समय की पितृसत्ता का सामना किया और यह साबित करने के लिए एक लंबी और दर्दनाक शारीरिक यात्रा की कि महिलाएं भी आध्यात्मिक मुक्ति प्राप्त करने में सक्षम हैं।
teaching_local: महिलाएं पुरुषों के समान ही जागृति की उच्चतम अवस्था तक पहुंचने में सक्षम हैं।
moral_local: बाधाओं के सामने दृढ़ता न केवल अपने लिए, बल्कि पीढ़ियों के लिए दरवाजे खोलती है।

name: Maharaja Ranjit Singh
tagline: The Lion of Punjab who built a secular empire uniting all faiths under the banner of justice.
journey: A child scarred by smallpox and blind in one eye, he rose to unite the warring Sikh misls into a formidable empire spanning from Tibet to the Afghan borders. He modernized the army, yet never instituted the death penalty. His court included Hindu, Muslim, and European ministers, creating a uniquely pluralistic and prosperous state.
trial: His trial was maintaining peace and unity in a highly volatile region fractured by religious violence, using immense strategic pragmatism and genuine secular tolerance to keep the British Empire at bay throughout his life.
teaching: God intended me to look upon all religions with one eye; that is why he took away the light from the other.
moral: True leadership elevates humanity beyond sectarian divides into shared prosperity.
journey_local: ਇੱਕ ਅੱਖ ਤੋਂ ਖੋਟੇ ਅਤੇ ਚੇਚਕ ਦੇ ਦਾਗਾਂ ਵਾਲੇ ਬੱਚੇ ਨੇ ਸਿੱਖ ਮਿਸਲਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਇਕਜੁੱਟ ਕਰਕੇ ਇੱਕ ਵਿਸ਼ਾਲ ਸਾਮਰਾਜ ਬਣਾਇਆ। ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੇ ਦਰਬਾਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸਾਰੇ ਧਰਮਾਂ ਦੇ ਮੰਤਰੀ ਸਨ।
trial_local: ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਦੀ ਪ੍ਰੀਖਿਆ ਧਾਰਮਿਕ ਹਿੰਸਾ ਨਾਲ ਟੁੱਟੇ ਹੋਏ ਖੇਤਰ ਵਿੱਚ ਸ਼ਾਂਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਏਕਤਾ ਬਣਾਈ ਰੱਖਣਾ ਸੀ।
teaching_local: ਪ੍ਰਮਾਤਮਾ ਨੇ ਮੈਨੂੰ ਸਾਰੇ ਧਰਮਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਇੱਕ ਅੱਖ ਨਾਲ ਵੇਖਣ ਲਈ ਕਿਹਾ ਹੈ; ਇਸੇ ਲਈ ਉਸਨੇ ਮੇਰੀ ਦੂਜੀ ਅੱਖ ਦੀ ਰੌਸ਼ਨੀ ਲੈ ਲਈ।
moral_local: ਸੱਚੀ ਲੀਡਰਸ਼ਿਪ ਮਨੁੱਖਤਾ ਨੂੰ ਸੰਪਰਦਾਇਕ ਵੰਡਾਂ ਤੋਂ ਉੱਪਰ ਉਠਾ ਕੇ ਸਾਂਝੀ ਖੁਸ਼ਹਾਲੀ ਵੱਲ ਲੈ ਜਾਂਦੀ ਹੈ।

name: Maharana Pratap
tagline: The unyielding King of Mewar who chose the hardships of the forest over submitting to an empire.
journey: Refusing to compromise the sovereignty of Mewar, he fought a relentless guerrilla war against the massive Mughal army, most famously at Haldighati.
trial: His trial was watching his family endure poverty in the jungles, yet his commitment to freedom outweighed comfort.
teaching: Freedom is the highest Dharma; it cannot be traded for gold.
moral: True nobility is tested in the wilderness of adversity.
journey_local: मेवाड़ की संप्रभुता से समझौता करने से इनकार करते हुए, उन्होंने मुगल सेना के खिलाफ युद्ध किया।
trial_local: उनकी परीक्षा अपने परिवार को जंगलों में गरीबी सहते हुए देखना था।
teaching_local: स्वतंत्रता सर्वोच्च धर्म है; इसे सोने के बदले नहीं बेचा जा सकता।
moral_local: सच्ची महानता की परीक्षा विपत्ति के जंगलों में होती है।

name: Mai Bhago
tagline: The fierce woman warrior who shamed deserters back into battle and became the Guru's bodyguard.
journey: During the grueling siege of Anandpur Sahib, 40 Sikhs signed a declaration abandoning Guru Gobind Singh and returned home. Mai Bhago, a devout village woman, was furious. She dressed in armor, mounted a horse, and challenged the men: "Either you stay here and act like women, or give me your clothes and I will go fight for the Guru." Shamed, the 40 men followed her back to the battlefield of Muktsar.
trial: She led the charge at the Battle of Muktsar, suffering severe wounds while fighting the vast Mughal army. She survived, while all 40 men achieved martyrdom (the Chali Mukte). She later dedicated her life as the personal bodyguard to Guru Gobind Singh.
teaching: Never abandon your Guru in times of hardship.
moral: Righteous indignation can awaken the dead conscience of an entire community.
journey_local: ਜਦੋਂ 40 ਸਿੱਖ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਨੂੰ ਛੱਡ ਕੇ ਘਰ ਆ ਗਏ, ਤਾਂ ਮਾਈ ਭਾਗੋ ਨੇ ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਸ਼ਰਮਿੰਦਾ ਕੀਤਾ ਅਤੇ ਵਾਪਸ ਮੁਕਤਸਰ ਦੀ ਜੰਗ ਵਿੱਚ ਲੈ ਗਈ।
trial_local: ਉਨ੍ਹਾਂ ਨੇ ਮੁਕਤਸਰ ਦੀ ਜੰਗ ਵਿੱਚ ਅਗਵਾਈ ਕੀਤੀ ਅਤੇ ਗੰਭੀਰ ਰੂਪ ਵਿੱਚ ਜ਼ਖਮੀ ਹੋਈ। ਬਾਅਦ ਵਿੱਚ ਉਹ ਗੁਰੂ ਜੀ ਦੀ ਅੰਗਰੱਖਿਅਕ ਬਣੀ।
teaching_local: ਔਖੇ ਸਮੇਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਕਦੇ ਵੀ ਆਪਣੇ ਗੁਰੂ ਦਾ ਸਾਥ ਨਾ ਛੱਡੋ।
moral_local: ਸੱਚਾ ਗੁੱਸਾ ਪੂਰੇ ਭਾਈਚਾਰੇ ਦੀ ਮਰੀ ਹੋਈ ਜ਼ਮੀਰ ਨੂੰ ਜਗਾ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ।

tagline: A Vedic woman whose story illustrates the theology and social life of her era.
